what_this_is: A dated measurement of every a2aregistry listing in the 2026-09-25 census frame (443 listings): whether its A2A agent card was served, and whether the card's signatures verify under a key the card itself points to, from one place.

read_state_vocabulary.EXHAUSTED: every listing of the frame reached exactly one state
read_state_vocabulary.PARTIAL: some listings were not read; counts are never a population total

units.listing: one a2aregistry entry in the census frame (registry uuid)
units.card: one JSON agent card served at a candidate URL (listing wellKnownURI, then <origin>/.well-known/agent-card.json, then agent.json)
units.signed card: a served card whose `signatures` array has at least one entry
units.percentages: denominator is cards served (CARD_SERVED), not listings

read.read_state_rule: EXHAUSTED only if every listing of the frame reached exactly one state

state_meanings.CARD_SERVED: a JSON object that parses as an agent card
state_meanings.AUTH_REQUIRED: 401/403 and no candidate served a card
state_meanings.UNREACHABLE: DNS, refused, TLS, reset, 5xx, or an off-host redirect only
state_meanings.ROBOTS_DISALLOWED: robots.txt forbids the card paths for CSOAI-census; only robots.txt was requested
state_meanings.NON_PUBLIC_ADDRESS: a candidate host resolves to a non-global address; not contacted
state_meanings.HF_SPACE_NOT_CONTACTED: every candidate is a *.hf.space host; not contacted

not_contacted.rule: no request to a host that resolves to a non-global address (checked for every candidate host) and none to *.hf.space (a request could wake a sleeping Space); robots.txt honoured

hf_space_listings.reason: listing.wellKnownURI: *.hf.space: the Space's sleep state was not checked and a request could wake it; not contacted (hf-spaces-mcp-probe.py reads the stage first); origin/.well-known/agent-card.json: dns: [Errno -3] Temporary failure in name resolution

not_contacted.hf_space_note: The one listing whose card URL is on *.hf.space is recorded UNREACHABLE, not HF_SPACE_NOT_CONTACTED, because its other candidate (an unqualified internal hostname from the listing's url) failed DNS. It received no request in this run; the DNS query for the internal name went to our resolver only.

cards_served.protocolVersion_note: what the card declares; no protocol negotiation took place and no A2A call was made

state_meanings.VERIFIED: at least one signature verifies under a key the card points to, and none fails. embedded_jwk = the card vouches for its own key: integrity, not identity
state_meanings.FAILED: a key was found and a signature did not verify under it over the payload the card's declared spec version defines
state_meanings.UNCHECKABLE: signatures present, but no key the card points to could be obtained; never counted as VERIFIED
state_meanings.NO_SIGNATURES: no `signatures` array, or an empty one

signatures.canonicalisation: per the spec version the card declares: 1.x (or nothing recognisable declared) = A2A spec 8.4.3 @ 72b3761 (default values removed per a2a.proto sha256 945df6e34001, `signatures` excluded, JCS RFC 8785); 0.x = JCS of the card with `signatures` excluded (the v0.3.0 spec defines no canonicalisation step); detached JWS (RFC 7515)
signatures.failed_note: FAILED = no verification under the key the card points to over the payload of the card's declared version; alt_serialisations_verifying (in correction.v0.1.1.evidence.json) is a diagnostic, never a pass

sent: GET <jku JWKS or did:web did.json> (only when a signature points to it)
never_sent: any request to a non-global address

protocol_note.a2a: protocolVersion figures are declarations in served cards, not negotiated versions
protocol_note.mcp: No MCP request is made by this census. For the sibling MCP censuses: the current MCP specification revision is 2026-07-28 (checked 2026-09-25), and our MCP probers request 2025-11-25.

anomalies.kind: DISCLOSED BREACH OF OUR OWN RULE (superseded run kept)
anomalies.what_we_say: Run 1 of this census (2026-09-25T07:18:59Z to 2026-09-25T07:19:54Z) applied the non-public-address check to the first candidate host only and did not exclude *.hf.space. It sent ONE request, GET /robots.txt, to vishalmysore-a2amcpdemo.hf.space without first reading the Space's stage from the Hub API - the stage check our rule requires. It also asked our resolver for the unqualified internal hostname in that listing; DNS failed and no connection was made. Run 1 is superseded by run 2 (this record) and kept for audit; its rows are not published as data.

space_stage_per_hub_api.read_by: huggingface.co/api/spaces/<id> (the Hub API, not the Space)
space_stage_per_hub_api.also_per_lane_note: SUPERSEDED.txt (run 1) records the Hub API reporting RUNTIME_ERROR after run 1
space_stage_per_hub_api.meaning: Both Hub API reads made after the request (the lane's, after run 1; this builder's, above) report RUNTIME_ERROR. The stage at the moment of the request was NOT read - that is the breach - so we cannot prove it; an errored Space is not started by a request the way a sleeping one is woken.

anomalies.fix: a2a-card-probe.py now address-checks every candidate host and never contacts *.hf.space (tests in test_a2a_card_probe.py)

anomalies.what_we_say: 2 served cards carry a `signatures` key with zero entries; they count as NO_SIGNATURES. So 35 cards have the key and 33 are signed.
7 listings the registry marks healthy served no card to us.
2 served cards are byte-identical to another listing's card (420 distinct of 422).
3 cards declare a protocolVersion different from their registry listing; declared values include strings that are not A2A release numbers (see cards_served.protocolVersion_declared).

not_evidence_of: that any agent works, is safe, is who it says, or does what its skills say
that a VERIFIED signature proves identity: it proves only that the key the card points to signed these bytes (embedded_jwk: integrity only)
that a FAILED or UNCHECKABLE card is malicious; it may be a canonicalisation or key-publication mistake
endorsement, ranking, grading, or approval of any agent or operator
a population total of A2A agents: the frame is one registry's listings on 2026-09-25
reachability at any other moment or from any other network location

verify.signature: record.v0.1.1.signed.json: canonicalise its payload (JSON, keys sorted, no whitespace, UTF-8); sha256 must equal signature.payload_sha256; payload.artifact.sha256 must equal sha256(record.v0.1.1.json); verify signature.sig_ed25519 (hex) with the #board-attestation-1 Ed25519 key in https://csoai.org/.well-known/did.json
verify.timestamp: record.v0.1.1.json.ots is an OpenTimestamps proof over sha256(record.v0.1.1.json). When published it was a PENDING calendar commitment; `ots upgrade` then `ots verify record.v0.1.1.json.ots` against a Bitcoin node decides whether it has become a Bitcoin attestation
verify.files: sha256 of every published file is in published_files and is pinned by the signature through record.json

supersedes.kept: record.json, record.signed.json, record.json.ots, record.ots.json, data/cards.jsonl.gz and every other 0.1 file stay published byte for byte: superseded, not deleted, not edited
